rationale: The sheet is visually coherent but too repetitive for a 20-option massing portfolio. All visible candidates stay inside one compact prismatic block lineage with minor variations in void depth and roof articulation, so the portfolio does not reach the required diversity of materially legible spatial families. The strongest reading is a neighborhood-block language with a controlled ground carve and one lifted threshold, but there is no evidence yet of at least ten distinct form/section families, nor a dominant-family cap below 30%. The next round should generate genuinely different mass relations: courtyard, bent bar, split wing, stepped mass, bridge, cross-mass, corner cut, and terrace-based variants that each preserve the active street edge and public void requirement while clearly changing section and silhouette.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: Single compact block family with similar street-facing footprint, similar upper-box massing, and only shallow void/notch variation; all read as one prismatic neighborhood block rather than distinct spatial types.

required_next_relations: courtyard or carve_void as a true usable public room, not just a surface dent

terrace or setback that shifts upper mass while preserving a calm base

split_wing or bent_bar to create a clearly different section and footprint from the main block family
